clue.text: Not concrete in any but the inference is there

definitions.text: Not concrete in any but the inference is there

parts.words: Not concrete in any but the inference is there
parts.note: describes proof that is never direct or tangible, yet points firmly to a conclusion a court may draw

explanation.surface: A remark about something abstract whose meaning can nonetheless be deduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect proof, from which guilt is inferred rather than shown outright, is the legal term described.

clue.text: Displays dissent about current charges

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
volts measure the electrical push behind a current

explanation.surface: Someone protests about the cost of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel or rise up is to show dissent in action.

clue.text: Lingo heard at the pearly-queen's party?

indicators.note: signals that the words are said out loud in a Cockney voice

parts.note: a pearly queen is a London Cockney figure; dropping the h, her do becomes 'er do

explanation.surface: Wondering what language is spoken at a Cockney celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are East London Cockney charity figures in button-covered costume; Cockneys drop the h, so 'her do' (her party) is said as 'er do.
explanation.definitionFit: A language of Pakistan and India, so a tongue or lingo.

clue.text: Native luminary ritual nudes can dress for

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange it, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Unclothed people at a ceremony may put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Plains Indian ceremony honouring the sun, the great luminary.

clue.text: A law is made for him

parts.note: lex is the Latin for law

explanation.surface: A statute drafted with one particular man in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so a fair stand-in for a male pronoun in this clue.

clue.text: Came to the conclusion no-one was at home

definitions.meaning: reasoned something through to the end, worked it all through
having called, you believed the residents away

explanation.definitionFit: Planned in full detail covers the first sense; supposed everyone absent covers the second.

clue.text: Slander in snake language

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Defaming someone in reptilian speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions on someone is to defame them.

clue.text: Feeling stronger than traitors' arms, according to Mark Antony

definitions.text: Feeling stronger than traitors' arms, according to Mark Antony

parts.words: Feeling stronger than traitors' arms, according to Mark Antony
parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Antony says Brutus's unkindness, more strong than traitors' arms, quite vanquished Caesar

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare about a sentiment that overpowered Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanklessness, the sin Antony names over Caesar's body in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: See 1
Portraitist prone to be devious

indicators.note: devious means winding off the straight path, so these letters stray into another order

explanation.surface: An artist who is inclined towards deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Orpen was an Irish painter famed for portraits.

clue.text: Bridge-work in the small hours

parts.note: a ship's officer on duty on the bridge between midnight and four in the morning

explanation.surface: Dentistry or a card game played late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval duty period from midnight to 4 a.m., kept on the ship's bridge.

clue.text: Man in the water

parts.note: the ... of Man sits in the Irish Sea, so Man here is a place surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: Someone swimming or drowning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the sea between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: His avoidance of duty is enough to rile German radical

definitions.text: His avoidance of duty is enough to rile German radical

indicators.note: radical means drastically altered, so these letters are thoroughly reorganised

explanation.surface: A shirker's idleness would anger a German extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker feigns illness to dodge work, which would anger anyone.

clue.text: One attractive in Billy Bunter's book?

definitions.text: One attractive in Billy Bunter's book?

parts.words: One attractive in Billy Bunter's book?
parts.note: Billy Bunter's stories ran in the boys' paper The Magnet, so its kind of attraction is magnetic

explanation.surface: Asking whether the fat schoolboy Billy Bunter found anyone appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Frank Richards's Greyfriars stories, first printed in the weekly paper The Magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes iron magnetic is literally an agent of attraction.

clue.text: Reserve in the long run

definitions.meaning: a race over a long course, as opposed to a sprint

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping people at arm's length is reserve; a long race is a distance event.

clue.text: Way in which setter strayed

indicators.note: strayed means wandered off course, so these letters wander into another order

explanation.surface: The route on which the compiler got lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or thoroughfare in a town.

clue.text: Robin, mud-splashed, near the end

indicators.note: splashed suggests letters scattered about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A muddy bird looks close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying, on the point of death.

clue.text: Girl bitter back in the European capital

indicators.note: back means the word for the beer is read from right to left

parts.note: bitter is a kind of ale

indicators.note: the capital or upper-case first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A girl comes home with a beer to a European capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, as of Tennyson's lily maid of Astolat.

clue.text: Old city with no liking for a Scottish expression

parts.note: anti means opposed to
och is a Scots exclamation

explanation.surface: An ancient city disliked by the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city of Syria, now Antakya in Turkey.

clue.text: Put on record

parts.note: to write something down formally so it is preserved, not to play a disc

explanation.definitionFit: To record in writing or by evidence.

clue.text: Give utterance to two points carrying little weight

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Speaking about two points that matter little.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce or state formally, to articulate.

clue.text: Army constructors' hint to save

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's construction corps
a cue is a prompt or hint

explanation.surface: Army engineers give a tip on how to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver from danger.

clue.text: Albeit a contrast the saint is in order

indicators.note: putting letters in order means sorting them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Musing that a holy person is properly placed despite being different.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct opposite or sharp contrast.

clue.text: Stimulant provided by travel commercial?

parts.note: to go is to travel
an ad is a commercial advertisement

explanation.surface: A holiday advertisement that makes you want to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur or prod that drives one on.

clue.text: Smart distinction I note

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British distinction
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A stylish touch of class marked by a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and elegant.

clue.text: Sounds cocky

parts.note: read as the noises a cockerel makes, not as an arrogant tone

explanation.definitionFit: A rooster's calls; also boasts.

clue.text: Social worker on the grass in a lying position

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: couch is a coarse grass
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A welfare officer relaxing on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic term for a beast lying down with head raised.

clue.text: But for whom Barkis would never have been willing

definitions.text: But for whom Barkis would never have been willing

parts.words: But for whom Barkis would never have been willing
parts.note: Barkis, the carrier in David Copperfield, says Barkis is willin'; without his author he would never have said it

explanation.surface: Someone without whom a reluctant man would not have consented.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist who created Barkis in David Copperfield.
